overview: The Medford School Committee governs the city's public school district, overseeing a broad portfolio that includes fiscal management, facility infrastructure, and student achievement standards. Meeting over a span from early 2023 through late 2026, the body has navigated significant challenges including major budget deficits, building failures, and the initial phases of a large-scale high school reconstruction project. The committee is responsible for approving labor contracts, setting district-wide policies on student conduct and inclusion, and appointing the Superintendent. As of late 2026, the body is focused on implementing a new community-led strategic plan, finalizing accelerated repairs for elementary schools, and progressing through the design phases of the Medford Comprehensive High School project.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a multi-year effort to rebuild or renovate Medford High School by submitting a Statement of Interest to the MSBA core program in 2023. After being invited into the eligibility phase, the body established a formal 15-member building committee and secured a project website at mhsproject.org to ensure transparency. In 2025, the committee selected the firm Left Field as its Owner's Project Manager and began a feasibility study that originally included 29 design alternatives. By 2026, the project team had to navigate a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgley Field that eliminated several design options, leading the committee to adopt modified schematic designs and explore LEED silver and net-zero energy goals.

threads.name: District Budget and Override Funding
threads.summary: The committee managed volatile fiscal conditions, starting with the approval of an operating budget in 2023 before facing a projected $2.5 million deficit in 2024 caused by structural underbudgeting and retroactive union settlements. Following the passage of local ballot questions 7 and 8, the body approved a supplemental budget appropriation to restore literacy coaches, behavioral specialists, and other previously cut positions. By 2026, the committee shifted focus to closing a $5 million gap for level services while debating whether stabilization funds should be considered part of the recurring base budget. Recent financial reports emphasize managing the rising costs of special education transportation and facility heating.

threads.name: HVAC Replacement and Facility Repairs
threads.summary: Widespread failures in aging cooling and heating systems forced the committee to prioritize massive capital infrastructure projects. In 2024, the body approved a $15 to $20 million scope for partial-decarbonization HVAC work at the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools, eventually approving a $25.7 million bond for comprehensive replacements. The committee also commissioned a facilities assessment identifying $83.7 million in needed repairs across five schools, including roof and floor tile failures. Most recently, the committee selected a ground-source geothermal heat pump system for the Missituk Elementary project and approved a Construction Manager at Risk model for the $22.7 million Roberts Elementary repairs.

threads.name: Elementary School Overcrowding and Space Planning
threads.summary: Severe enrollment disparities at the Roberts Elementary School prompted a prolonged debate regarding district redistricting and school grade configurations. In early 2025, the committee voted to relocate preschool classrooms from the Roberts to the Missituk to create space, while tasking a subcommittee to study long-term enrollment buffers. The body reviewed a consultant's recommendation to restructure schools into K-4, 5-6, and 7-8 grade spans to alleviate overcrowding. However, citing the need for better financial and construction coordination, the committee voted in 2026 to delay any grade configuration changes until at least the 2028-2029 school year.

threads.name: After-School Programming Expansion
threads.summary: Addressing significant waitlists for before and after-school care was a consistent priority, beginning with the 2023 decision to replace traditional waitlists with a lottery system. The committee authorized tuition and staff pay increases to stabilize the program and partnered with the BASIC collaborative to identify expansion opportunities. In 2026, the committee approved a restructuring that added 150 seats, transitioned site coordinators to full-time roles, and introduced a 4:00 p.m. early-pickup option for families. By late 2026, the district reported a 68% reduction in the program's waitlist compared to previous years.

threads.name: Superintendent Transitions and Leadership
threads.summary: The body managed the leadership transition following the seven-year tenure of Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent, who departed in early 2025. Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi was appointed to the interim role and tasked with stabilizing the district through contract negotiations and the high school building project. After a year under interim leadership, and following positive performance evaluations and public input regarding district stability, the committee voted in early 2026 to appoint Galusi as the permanent superintendent. A three-year contract was subsequently approved, aligning the superintendent’s evaluation cadence with the academic school year.

threads.name: Academic Standards and AI Integration
threads.summary: The committee modernized district academics by adopting the Houghton Mifflin Harcourt 'Into Reading' curriculum and revising graduation requirements. Following the state's removal of the MCAS graduation mandate, the committee updated its competency policy to focus on the successful completion of aligned coursework in core subjects. The body also took a proactive stance on emerging technology by adopting a formal policy on generative artificial intelligence in schools. This policy regulates ethical use for students and explicitly prohibits educators from using AI tools to grade or provide feedback on qualitative student work.

threads.name: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)
threads.summary: Inclusion initiatives focused on codifying protections for LGBTQ+ students and staff and formalizing the district's DEI infrastructure. The committee approved a comprehensive non-discrimination policy regarding gender identity, facility access, and records, and reaffirmed its support for the rights of LGBTQIA+ community members. Structurally, the committee recommended the creation of a dedicated school-based DEI director position to manage culture and discipline independently of the city's DEI office. Recently, the body passed resolutions supporting students and staff affected by Temporary Protected Status (TPS) terminations and ensuring continued privacy standards.
